comments.comment: 17:58  Hancock's not really up to speed with his PC interpretation of hunter gatherers. If evidence exists that hunter gatherers with stone age tech have wiped out entire species of megafauna than the possibility that it happened more than once is on the table. Sure enough, it did. The New Zealand Maori were only in NZ for 400 years before the first Europeans arrived and in just the first 100 they had wiped out all the giant Moa bird varieties (some of them as big as cattle) that filled the landscape. By the time Europeans arrived they'd also destroyed 50% of all the forests and 50% of all endemic species had been made extinct, including the giant eagles that preyed on the Moa. Everything that remained from the rape of the landscape by these Polynesian colonists was either good at running from them, hiding from them, flying away from them or just too much trouble to catch or burn down.  Easter Island is an even more extreme example of the same mentality. Hunter gatherers are generally restricted in the amount of destruction they can cause by lack of technology not an imagined hippy dippy mindset. Efficient farming techniques introduced by Europeans saved what was left in NZ. Even when some native species were still threatened with extinction, Maori complained that not letting them eat the few that were left was culturally insensitive. How's that for a fucking self absorbed mentality?
